scenes.title: VPC address space, subnets and routes
scenes.visual_overview: This original slide illustrates vpc address space, subnets and routes with AWS network topology and explicit route examples.
visual_walkthrough: Identify VPC and subnet or gateway boundaries

The left diagram shows VPC ten dot twenty dot zero dot zero slash sixteen split across two Availability Zones. Each zone contains a public and private subnet, with different nonoverlapping slash twenty-four ranges. A VPC CIDR allocates the broader IP address space, but each subnet is confined to one Availability Zone. On the right the route table maps a destination CIDR to a next hop, such as local delivery or an Internet Gateway. Read both the VPC boundary and the subnet route table before deciding where packets can go.

A working traffic path also needs matching security groups and network ACLs; a route alone does not grant permission.

For a professional architecture decision, inspect the source and destination addresses, the effective route table associated with the subnet, and the security boundaries. A correct route without the right policy or a return path does not prove end-to-end connectivity. Treat the concrete values in the diagram as a worked example of this decision, not as a configuration that every workload must reuse.

scenes.title: Public, private and isolated subnets
scenes.visual_overview: This original slide illustrates public, private and isolated subnets with AWS network topology and explicit route examples.
visual_walkthrough: Identify VPC and subnet or gateway boundaries

The slide compares three route tables. The public subnet sends a default IPv4 route to an Internet Gateway, but a resource also needs a public address and permitting security rules for direct IPv4 internet access. The private subnet sends its default route to a NAT Gateway placed in a public subnet, allowing outbound-initiated IPv4 traffic and return packets but not unsolicited inbound internet connections. The isolated subnet contains only local routes, so it cannot reach the public internet through these paths. The lower note recommends NAT Gateways per Availability Zone when resilience and cross-AZ costs matter.
Walk through the real CIDRs, next hops and security constraints
The public or private label describes routing choices, not automatic security-group or internet reachability.

scenes.title: Internet Gateway, NAT Gateway and egress-only IGW
scenes.visual_overview: This original slide illustrates internet gateway, nat gateway and egress-only igw with AWS network topology and explicit route examples.
visual_walkthrough: Identify VPC and subnet or gateway boundaries

Three independent paths are shown. A public IPv4 EC2 instance with a public address and a default route through an Internet Gateway can communicate directly with the internet when allowed by security controls. A private IPv4 instance instead uses a NAT Gateway in a public subnet for outbound-initiated traffic; the NAT performs source IPv4 address translation. An IPv6-only private outbound path can use an egress-only Internet Gateway with a double-colon slash zero route, preventing unsolicited inbound IPv6 sessions but not performing NAT. Read the address family, next hop, and whether inbound access is required.
Walk through the real CIDRs, next hops and security constraints
Choose the correct internet exit for IPv4 versus IPv6 and avoid confusing egress-only IPv6 routing with NAT.
